response.sql: WITH order_counts AS (SELECT account_id, COUNT(*) AS number_of_orders FROM `order` GROUP BY account_id), account_regions AS (SELECT DISTINCT disp.account_id, district.A3 AS region FROM disp JOIN client ON client.client_id = disp.client_id JOIN district ON district.district_id = client.district_id WHERE disp.type = 'OWNER'), counts AS (SELECT oc.account_id, ar.region, oc.number_of_orders FROM order_counts AS oc JOIN account_regions AS ar ON ar.account_id = oc.account_id), differences AS (SELECT account_id, region, number_of_orders, number_of_orders - AVG(number_of_orders) OVER () AS difference_from_overall_average FROM counts), regional AS (SELECT *, AVG(difference_from_overall_average) OVER (PARTITION BY region) AS region_average_difference FROM differences) SELECT account_id, region, number_of_orders, difference_from_overall_average, difference_from_overall_average - region_average_difference AS excess_over_region_average FROM regional WHERE difference_from_overall_average > region_average_difference ORDER BY excess_over_region_average DESC LIMIT 10

assumptions.assumption: Each account has one owner; the schema does not enforce this. Duplicate owner records in the same region are collapsed into one account–region row.
